name: ClubPlanner
tagline: Belgian club management software for gyms and fitness centers: members, subscriptions, class schedules, recurring billing and door access.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Vendor sells per club, likely quoted.

verdictSummary: This is not a personal productivity app, it is the operational spine of a gym: membership contracts, recurring SEPA collection, failed payment chasing, class bookings, staff roles and badge readers on the front door. An agent can absolutely produce a member database with a class calendar and a check-in screen in a weekend, and that part is genuinely easy. What it cannot produce is a direct debit mandate flow that a Belgian bank and your accountant both accept, or a driver for the turnstile you already bought. The moment real money and real doors are involved, the boring parts are the entire product. Build the roster if you run a tiny volunteer club, otherwise pay.
coreLoopDIY: A local members and classes database with subscription records, a class schedule, and a tablet check-in screen that logs attendance.
requirements: a machine or small VPS to run it on
a tablet or laptop at the front desk
manual bank reconciliation, or a payment provider account if you want real collection
whatYouLose: SEPA direct debit collection with mandates, retries and dunning on failed payments
Integration with access control hardware: badges, turnstiles, gate relays
Member-facing app and online signup, so people book classes themselves instead of asking you
Accountant-friendly invoicing, VAT handling and export to Belgian bookkeeping tools
Someone else holding the GDPR liability for a database of names, bodies and payment details
moatNotes: Recurring collection plus physical door hardware is a nasty combination to replicate, and gyms migrate systems roughly never.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the software is not the point, the cash flow is. A club with 600 members needs money to arrive every month without a human touching it, needs the failures flagged, needs the door to stop opening when someone stops paying, and needs a number to call when any of that breaks at 7am on a Monday. A self-built roster gives you the pretty part and leaves you personally holding the billing, the hardware and the data protection exposure. That trade only makes sense at a very small scale.
notes: The member list is a weekend, the direct debit and the turnstile are not. The moat is recurring collection plumbing wired to physical hardware, sitting under a business that cannot afford a bad migration.
prompt:
Build a small self-hosted club management app for a single-location sports or fitness club. One admin, no public signup, no cloud services.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js (App Router) with TypeScript and Tailwind
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/club.db, migrations as plain SQL files run on boot
- Single shared password from ADMIN_PASSWORD in .env, checked in middleware, session in a signed cookie
- No external APIs, no telemetry, no analytics

Data model:
- members: name, email, phone, birthdate, joined_on, status (active | paused | ended), notes
- membership_plans: name, price_cents, billing_period (monthly | quarterly | yearly), class_credits_per_period (nullable = unlimited)
- subscriptions: member, plan, start_date, end_date (nullable), status
- payments: subscription, period_start, period_end, amount_cents, due_on, status (due | paid | failed), paid_on, method (cash | transfer | card)
- classes: title, coach name, weekday, start_time, duration_minutes, capacity, active flag
- sessions: generated occurrences of a class for a given date
- attendance: member, session, checked_in_at

Screens:
1. Members list with search and status filter, member detail page showing subscription, payment history and attendance history
2. Plans and subscriptions CRUD
3. Billing page: a button that generates due payment rows for the current period from active subscriptions (idempotent, never double-generate for the same period), plus a list of overdue payments and a one-click mark-as-paid
4. Schedule page: weekly grid of classes, generate sessions for the next 4 weeks, book members into a session up to capacity
5. Kiosk check-in page at /kiosk: big search box, type a name, tap to check into today's session, shows a red banner if the member has an overdue payment
6. CSV export of members and of payments

Explicitly out of scope, do not attempt: direct debit or card collection, invoice PDFs, VAT logic, email or SMS sending, access control hardware, member self-service accounts, multi-location, multi-staff roles.

Seed the database with 3 plans, 25 fake members and 6 weekly classes so the app is explorable immediately. Include a README with setup, .env.example, and a one-line nightly backup command that copies the SQLite file with a timestamp.
